# `ranges.aug`

<a id="symbol-RangeError"></a>
## `RangeError` · class · [source](ranges.aug#L3)

A range has an invalid step or exceeds its explicit allocation limit. It implements `Error`. It takes `message` as a string, kept read-only.

<a id="symbol-range"></a>
## `range` · [source](ranges.aug#L13)

Return a new list of integers from start up to, but excluding, end.
A step past the int64 boundary stops before producing a wrapped value.

It takes `end` as an integer (Exclusive boundary), `start` as an integer (when omitted, `0`) (First value, default 0), `step` as an integer (when omitted, `1`) (Nonzero increment, default 1; a negative step descends), and `limit` as an integer (when omitted, `1000000`) (Maximum number of allocated elements, default 1000000; permitted from 1 to 1000000). Failures can raise [`RangeError`](ranges.aug.md#symbol-RangeError) (Invalid step, invalid limit, or too many elements).

If `step` equals `0`, it raises a [`RangeError`](ranges.aug.md#symbol-RangeError) with `message` `"Range step must not be zero"`. If `limit` is less than `1` or `limit` is greater than `1000000`, it raises a [`RangeError`](ranges.aug.md#symbol-RangeError) with `message` `"Range limit must be from 1 to 1000000"`. It sets `values` of type `List<int>` to a list with no items. It sets `current` to `start`.

While (`step` is positive and `current` is less than `end`) or (`step` is negative and `current` is greater than `end`), if the number of elements in `values` equals `limit`, it raises a [`RangeError`](ranges.aug.md#symbol-RangeError) with `message` `"Range exceeds its element limit"`. With temporary permission to change `values`, it appends `current` to `values`. It sets `nextValue` to `current` plus `step`. If (`step` is positive and `nextValue` is less than `current`) or (`step` is negative and `nextValue` is greater than `current`), it leaves the nearest loop after cleanup.

It sets `current` to `nextValue`. After the loop, it returns `values`.

Built-in operations follow the [language reference](https://greenpandastudios.github.io/augscript/language-constructs).
